title: Ramona Sky
subtitle: Staggs family, 740 Progress Lane, Ramona, CA, 1903-2026
label: Staggs family, 740 Progress Lane, Ramona, CA
location_lines: Staggs family, 740 Progress Lane, Ramona, CA
T13S R1E, San Bernardino Meridian, inside the former Rancho Santa María (Valle de Pamo) grant; never sectioned, so no federal homestead patent
Santa Maria Valley, about 2 km SSE of Ramona's historic Main Street, at about 1,490 ft
intro: 1843-11-25: Gov. Micheltorena grants Rancho Valle de Pamo / Santa María (4 leagues) to José Joaquín Ortega and Edward Stokes.
1872-07-30: US patent to Ortega et al. for 17,708.85 acres, the root of title for the lot.
1869-70: gold is found at Julian, ~24 km ENE. The Julian wagon road ran through the valley.
1883: Amos Verlaque builds a store and post office on the Julian road; the settlement is called Nuevo.
1886: Milton Santee's Santa Maria Land & Water Co. subdivides the valley and names it Ramona, after Helen Hunt Jackson's novel.
1895-06-18: the post office name settles on Ramona for good.
1974-75: Progress Lane appears as a graded track.
1975-77: the first structure appears on the lot; the house is clear by 1980 and mapped on the 1982 USGS revision.
2003 Cedar fire: nearest edge ~1.6 km SE. 2007 Witch fire: nearest edge ~1.1 km E. The lot did not burn.
2006: the Ramona Valley becomes a wine AVA.
owners: Kumeyaay homeland; Mission San Diego sphere
Rancho grantees J. J. Ortega and E. Stokes (Stokes died 1847)
US patent to José Joaquín Ortega et al.
Santa Maria Land & Water Co. subdivides the Ramona townsite. Whether this lot was in its tract is likely but unverified.
owners_note: Ownership history: research in progress. The chain of title from the 1872 patent to the present is unknown.
